output.summary: A perennial flowering plant found across most of Europe and not native to North America, wood dock favours damp, shady places, especially woodland. One variety has striking bright-red leaf veins, while another is entirely green. Its preferably young leaves are eaten, including in salads, but oxalates make large quantities inadvisable.
output.edibilityNote: Preferably young leaves are eaten raw in salads or as a wild vegetable, but harmful oxalates mean large quantities should be avoided.
